problem: Visual Navigation Models (GNM, ViNT, NoMaD, NaviBridger, CrossFormer) are evaluated almost only by success rate, which hides trajectory quality, collisions, goal-recognition errors and robustness. Real-world zero-shot behavior is poorly understood.
motivation: VNMs are being deployed on real robots, but their failures cannot be explained or predicted. Richer metrics (path, vision-based, perturbation robustness) are needed to diagnose why models fail across embodiments and environments.
key_idea: Benchmark five pretrained VNMs zero-shot on two real robots in five indoor/outdoor environments using path metrics, image-similarity goal-recognition metrics, and controlled image perturbations.
insight: Newer, more complex transformer/diffusion models do not beat the simple GNM: it often matches or beats them on perceptual metrics (LPIPS/DreamSim) and does better in the OOD Snow setting. Frequent collisions (e.g. Corridor: NoMaD 3/3, CrossFormer 3/3, NaviBridger 2/3, vs 0/3 for GNM and ViNT) suggest weak geometric understanding, and repeated visual features cause premature goal predictions (Arena). The authors argue data, not architecture, is the bottleneck, but this is a hypothesis with no controlled test.
method: Models evaluated: GNM (MobileNetV2 + FC), ViNT (EfficientNet-B0 + Transformer), NoMaD (diffusion + goal masking), NaviBridger (diffusion bridge with learned prior), CrossFormer (transformer with embodiment-specific heads); all use open-source pretrained weights exported to ONNX for onboard inference.

Topological-map deployment: a reference trajectory is teleoperated with an RGB fisheye camera and LiDAR-based SLAM poses; images are sampled at fixed intervals to build a linear topomap and the last node is the goal.

Environments and robots: Corridor (3.749 m, Bunker), Office loop (27.96 m, Bunker), Stairs (6.247 m, Spot), Arena (20.05 m, Spot), and Snow (18.96 m, Bunker; OOD). Spot's built-in controller avoids collisions; Bunker has no collision avoidance.

Navigation metrics: remaining distance to goal (via checkpoints along the reference), path length, collision occurrence (trial ends at the first collision), goal-prediction count, and topological node error.
Vision metrics: LPIPS, DreamSim (called DSSIM in the paper), and PSNR between the final observation and the goal image on goal-predicted trials.
Perturbation tests: motion blur and sunflare are applied to the topomap images in Corridor, only for models that succeeded in the standard Corridor (GNM, ViNT).

setting.backbone: GNM, ViNT, NoMaD, NaviBridger, CrossFormer (pretrained, frozen, open-source weights)
setting.training_data: none (zero-shot evaluation of pretrained models, originally trained on robot datasets like RECON, GO Stanford, TartanDrive, SCAND)
setting.observation: monocular RGB fisheye camera image history plus goal image (topological map of images)
setting.action_space: predicted waypoints / waypoint trajectories with temporal distance, executed by the robot's low-level controller
setting.privileged: none at test time (LiDAR SLAM poses used only for evaluation and for recording the reference trajectory)

numbers_note: No standard-benchmark results are reported; this is a real-world evaluation of five VNMs on a custom dataset. Per-model, per-environment results are in tables and are baselines, not the paper's own method. They are not entered here.
results: Only GNM and ViNT succeed in all 3 Corridor trials without collision, while NoMaD, NaviBridger and CrossFormer collide. In the Office loop, collisions are 5/10 for GNM, 1/10 for ViNT, 2/10 for NoMaD and 9/10 for NaviBridger. In Snow, GNM has the lowest goal distance (1.12) versus ViNT 9.96 and NoMaD 10.76; in Arena, ViNT, NoMaD and CrossFormer show many premature or missed goal predictions.
limitations: Few trials per setting (3-10) and only 5 environments, so results have high variance.
Confounds: different robots per environment, weather and lighting in Snow, and reasons for failures (data vs. architecture) are hypothesized rather than tested.
No social navigation; perturbations applied only to the topomap in Corridor and only for GNM and ViNT.
